question.text: FPIs are NOT allowed to issue Offshore Derivative Instruments (ODIs) referencing which of the following?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI FPI framework, FPIs shall not issue ODIs referencing derivatives, and they shall not hedge their ODIs with derivative positions on stock exchanges in India. These restrictions apply subject to specified separate-registration exceptions. The Trap: ODIs referencing equity shares are permitted under the framework, but only subject to separate-registration and position-limit conditions - so a blanket "equity shares ODIs are unrestricted" reading would be wrong. Note: The core rule is ODIs + derivatives = not permitted; ODIs + equity shares = permitted but conditional on the separate-registration and position-limit requirements of the FPI master circular.
